title: Overtraining syndrome: a practical guide
claims: Overtraining syndrome is described as a maladapted response to excessive exercise without adequate rest, involving neurological, endocrine and immune systems and mood changes.
Persistent fatigue and a decline or plateau in performance should prompt consideration of overtraining syndrome and exclusion of underlying illness.
There is no single diagnostic marker; assessment is clinical and requires identifying contributing training, recovery and health factors.
Management includes rest and correction of the factors that led to the imbalance between training and recovery.

Functional overreaching is a temporary performance decrement that improves after rest (days to weeks) with super-compensation; nonfunctional overreaching and OTS involve longer decrement, with OTS recovery measured in weeks to months.

By some definitions, fewer than 14 to 21 days of rest to return to previous performance is classified as NFO, and more than 14 to 21 days as OTS; the boundary can often only be made retrospectively, based on time to recovery rather than symptom degree or type.
Resting heart rate, maximal heart rate and HRV do not show consistent results and do not differentiate FO, NFO and OTS; there are no specific and validated blood markers for NFO or OTS.
Potential triggers include increased training load without adequate recovery, training monotony, excessive competitions, sleep disturbances and personal-life stressors.
One of the initial signs of overreaching is an increased rating of perceived exertion for a given workload.

FO needs only balancing overload training with appropriate recovery; treatment of NFO and OTS is rest (some propose relative rest), rebuilding volume before intensity, starting from 5 to 10 minutes daily until 1 hour is tolerated; which strategy is best remains unclear.

A clinical history suggestive of NFO/OTS should show decreased performance persisting despite weeks to months of recovery, mood disturbances, and absence of signs, symptoms or diagnosis of other possible causes of underperformance.
